Subject: Hosted evaluation: sandbox endpoints, traffic buckets, and deployment decision items

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before I spin up sandbox access:

Recap of your priorities from the call:
- Low-latency conversational assistant for customer support (target 95th perc latency < 350ms)
- Initial traffic: ~120 concurrent agents during peak hours, ~3k API calls/minute peak across users
- Data residency: US-only production; eval data can live in hosted sandbox
- Security: need SOC 2 evidence + audit log access for the pilot

Recommendation (high level): start with a hosted evaluation run so you can validate latency, cost, and prompt quality quickly. If you later need strict network isolation or guaranteed throughput, we can map a Dedicated capacity proposal or a Private VPC path.

What I will provide this week:
- Sandbox endpoints and test tokens (two endpoints: chat-heavy and chat-cost-optimized) — see attached runbook
- Example traffic buckets and a suggested load profile to exercise prefix caching and batching
- SOC 2 summary + pointer to our security questionnaire for your compliance team

Asks for you / your infra lead:
1) Confirm whether the initial eval traffic above (3k rpm, 120 concurrent) is accurate or if you expect larger burst behavior.
2) Confirm any IP allowlist needs for sandbox egress (we can provide a CIDR block).
3) Tell us who on your side will be the contact for security docs (name + email).

If that all sounds good I’ll send sandbox credentials and schedule a 30-min preflight with one of our Solutions Engineers (Jordan) to walk through the runbook.

Thanks — Monica

Thanks Monica — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Traffic profile: the 3k rpm estimate is correct for the first week of pilot. We expect spikes up to ~6k rpm for short bursts (30-90s) when promos hit. Concurrency probably 100–150.
2) Latency SLO: 95th < 350ms is our goal in production. For evaluation we can tolerate 2x that while we tune.
3) Data residency: production must be US-only. Sandbox can be in hosted us-west or us-east.
4) Security contact: Priya N. (priya.n@brightlinefoods.com) — she will lead the questionnaire and review SOC2 docs.

One ask: if we start hosted, what does a transparent fallback look like if latency or capacity becomes an issue? We may prefer a hybrid where critical flows route to Dedicated if needed.

—Samir

Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: sandbox endpoints, traffic buckets, and deployment decision items

Great — thanks for the details, Samir. A couple of clarifications and concrete mapping so your infra team can evaluate tradeoffs:

Why start with Hosted (recommended pilot path)
- Fastest time-to-validate prompt quality and latency without provisioning GPUs or dealing with KMS keys
- We provide two sandbox endpoints so you can replicate both high-throughput and cost-optimized patterns:
  • chat-heavy-us-west (optimised for low latency, higher cost per token)
  • chat-cost-us-west (quantized model variant, lower cost, slightly higher median latency)
- Automatic batching + prefix KV caching enabled in sandbox so your observed token cost will be representative of hosted economics.

Dedicated vs Private (short tradeoff notes)
- Dedicated: guaranteed throughput and pinning of GPU pools; good if you need consistent 95th pct latency at scale. Requires commit/contract.
- Private VPC/On-prem: required when you must control network egress, HSM-backed keys, or air-gapped setups. Longer lead time and on-prem infra ops.

Fallback and routing options (how hybrid would work)
- Smart routing: you can configure a primary route to Hosted endpoints and an automated fallback to a Dedicated pool (or alternate region) if we detect latency regressions or throttling. We can include a canary policy in the pilot.

Sandbox rate guidance (examples to test capacity and caching benefits)
- Per-user call ceiling: 60 requests/minute (simulate agent interactions)
- Account-level sustained target: 3k rpm with 6k rpm burst allowed during promo windows (we’ll provide a load script)
- Account token-level qps: plan for 150 qps sustained to exercise batching and KV cache hits

Next steps I’ll take this week:
1) Share sandbox credentials and the Brightline quickstart runbook (attached).
2) Jordan will schedule a 30-minute preflight with Priya to walk the security checklist and confirm IP allowlist needs.
3) Aditya will prepare an optional Dedicated pricing sketch in case you want a throughput guarantee after pilot.

Let me know preferred times for the preflight (Jordan copied) and I’ll push credentials.

Best — Monica
